title: Online social activity time predicts ADHD problems in youth from late childhood to early adolescence in the ABCD study
authors: Deng H, Song K, Geng X, Xu L, Zhang J, Li X, He J, Potenza MN, Zhang J

primary_models.name: Random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) of OSA time (texting + social networking + video chat) and CBCL ADHD problems across four annual waves, full sample, adjusted for demographics and video-centric screen time
primary_models.location_in_paper: Fig. 1 (p. 2199), standardized within-person cross-lagged paths and between-person random-intercept correlation; model fit in Results p. 2198; interpreted in Results p. 2199 and Discussion p. 2200. Full parameter tables are in supplementary Tables S2 and S3, which are not bundled in the PDF.
primary_models.design: Longitudinal, four annual ABCD waves: baseline T1 (2016-2018, ages 9-10), 1-year follow-up T2 (2017-2019), 2-year follow-up T3 (2018-2020), 3-year follow-up T4 (2019-2021). OSA time and ADHD problems are measured at every wave. The RI-CLPM separates stable between-person differences (random intercepts for OSA and ADHD, allowed to correlate) from within-person wave-to-wave deviations. The within-person part has autoregressive paths, lag-specific cross-lagged paths in both directions (OSA t -> ADHD t+1 and ADHD t -> OSA t+1, freely estimated per lag, not constrained equal), and within-wave residual correlations. OSA time is the IV in the OSA -> ADHD paths and the DV in the ADHD -> OSA paths. Pre-registered at OSF (10.17605/OSF.IO/KXYZP).
primary_models.sample: ABCD Release 5.0. 11,868 enrolled at baseline; 43 excluded for missing baseline OSA time and 8 for missing baseline ADHD problems, leaving N = 11,819 analyzed with FIML. Wave-specific available N (Table 2): OSA time 11,819 / 11,157 / 10,884 / 10,259 and ADHD 11,819 / 11,165 / 8,053 / 7,428 at T1-T4. Baseline mean age 9.92 (SD 0.62). 6,163 male (52.1%), 5,656 female (47.9%). Race: White 7,587 (64.2%), Black 1,865 (15.8%), Asian 273 (2.3%), Mixed/Other 2,094 (17.7%). Hispanic 2,392 (20.2%). Parents married or living with partner 73.5%; parental college education 72.7%. Family income <$25,000 18.0% through $200,000+ 10.6% (Table 1).
primary_models.iv: Online social activity (OSA) time from the ABCD Youth Screen Time Survey: youth-reported time on 'texting', 'visiting social networking sites' and 'video chatting', summed, for weekdays and weekends, then combined as ((weekday*5) + (weekend*2))/7 to give typical daily time. The composite is built only from phone/SM items, so it qualifies under FT-IC2 Step 2. Units are not stated explicitly but follow the survey's hours-per-day metric. Table 1 means (SD): T1 0.54 (1.15), T2 0.89 (1.57), T3 1.58 (2.15), T4 2.44 (2.63). In the ADHD -> OSA paths this same variable is the DV.
primary_models.dv: ADHD problems: parent-reported CBCL attention problems syndrome subscale (items rated 0-2), analyzed as CBCL T-scores. Table 1 means (SD): T1 53.90 (6.17), T2 53.71 (5.98), T3 53.47 (5.58), T4 53.61 (5.62). In the ADHD -> OSA paths ADHD problems is the predictor.

covariates.name: Parental marital status
covariates.detail: Time-invariant; single vs married/living with partner

covariates.name: Highest level of parental education
covariates.detail: Time-invariant; high school or less vs college

covariates.name: Video-centric activity (VCA) time
covariates.detail: Time-varying covariate at each wave: summed time watching TV shows or movies, watching videos and playing videogames; at T3 only TV/movies + videogames because 'watching videos' was not measured. Table 1 means (SD): T1 3.26 (2.48), T2 3.60 (2.62), T3 4.03 (2.71), T4 3.77 (2.17)

primary_models.equation: Between level: OSA[i,t] = mu_OSA[t] + RI_OSA[i] + w_OSA[i,t]; ADHD[i,t] = mu_ADHD[t] + RI_ADHD[i] + w_ADHD[i,t]; cov(RI_OSA, RI_ADHD) estimated. Within level for t = 1..3: w_OSA[i,t+1] = a_t*w_OSA[i,t] + c_t*w_ADHD[i,t] + u_OSA[i,t+1]; w_ADHD[i,t+1] = b_t*w_ADHD[i,t] + d_t*w_OSA[i,t] + u_ADHD[i,t+1]; cov(w_OSA[i,1], w_ADHD[i,1]) and cov(u_OSA[i,t], u_ADHD[i,t]) estimated. Time-invariant covariates (age, sex, race, ethnicity, marital status, parental education, income) and time-varying VCA time enter as predictors; exact placement of covariates in the model is not described. Focal effects: d_t (OSA -> ADHD) and c_t (ADHD -> OSA), reported as standardized coefficients.
primary_models.estimation: SEM software not named (covariate imputation in R v4.3.1, mice v3.16.0). Maximum likelihood robust (MLR) estimator; missing outcome data handled with FIML. Missing covariates (age 0.01%, race 1.43%, ethnicity 1.29%, marital status 0.81%, parental education 0.12%, income 8.57%) imputed by chained equations, 100 imputations combined into one dataset using modes (categorical) and medians (continuous); supplementary materials repeat analyses on the non-imputed data. No survey weights and no site or family clustering reported. Fit: CFI = 0.953, TLI = 0.920, RMSEA = 0.040, SRMR = 0.044, chi-square(102) = 2028.860, p < 0.001. Significance flagged as *p <= 0.05, **p <= 0.01, ***p <= 0.001; no multiple-comparison correction. Moderation by sex and by OSA content type (video- vs image-based most-used platform) tested with multigroup models compared against cross-lag-constrained models via Satorra-Bentler chi-square tests (sex: see M2; content type: no moderation, Table S5-S7).

primary_models.name: Sex multigroup RI-CLPM of OSA time and CBCL ADHD problems (females vs males), same covariates as M1
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 3 (p. 2200); constraint tests in supplementary Tables S8 and S9 (not in PDF); interpreted in Results p. 2199 and Discussion p. 2201.
primary_models.design: Same four-wave RI-CLPM structure as M1 (T1-T4, annual), estimated as a multigroup model with females and males as groups and cross-lagged paths free across groups. Compared with a model constraining cross-lagged paths equal across sex; the Satorra-Bentler test indicated group differences, so group-specific cross-lags are reported. OSA time is the IV in the OSA -> ADHD paths and the DV in the ADHD -> OSA paths.
primary_models.sample: Same N = 11,819 as M1, split into females N = 5,656 and males N = 6,163 (Table 3).
primary_models.iv: Same OSA time composite as M1 (texting + social networking sites + video chat, weighted daily average). Sex-specific descriptive statistics are not reported in the main text.
primary_models.dv: Same CBCL attention problems T-score as M1. Sex-specific descriptive statistics are not reported in the main text.

covariates.name: Same covariates as M1
covariates.detail: Baseline age, race, ethnicity, parental marital status, parental education, family income (time-invariant) and video-centric activity time (time-varying). The paper does not say whether sex was dropped as a covariate in the sex multigroup model.

primary_models.equation: Same within- and between-person structure as M1, estimated separately per group g in {female, male} with free cross-lags: w_ADHD[i,t+1] = b_t,g*w_ADHD[i,t] + d_t,g*w_OSA[i,t] + u; w_OSA[i,t+1] = a_t,g*w_OSA[i,t] + c_t,g*w_ADHD[i,t] + u. Focal effects d_t,g and c_t,g, reported as standardized coefficients.
primary_models.estimation: As M1: MLR estimator, FIML, imputed covariates, software for the SEM not named. Moderation tested with a Satorra-Bentler chi-square difference test between an unconstrained multigroup model and one with cross-lagged paths constrained equal across sex. Table 3 reports beta, SE, 95% CI and exact p; bold marks CIs not overlapping zero (p < 0.05). No multiple-comparison correction.

d_transformation.conversion_formula: Standardized beta treated as approximate r: d = 2 * beta_std / sqrt(1 - beta_std^2) (Borenstein et al. 2009 eq 7.1). Applied to CI endpoints where CIs are printed (M2 only).
d_transformation.contrast_type: Per 1 within-person SD of the predictor (deviation from the child's own mean) at wave t, predicting the within-person SD of the outcome at wave t+1, net of the autoregressive path and covariates. The between-person cell is a correlation of stable person-level means.
d_transformation.notes: No SD_IV or SD_DV is needed because the paper reports standardized coefficients. For reference, Table 1 (p. 2198) gives OSA time SDs 1.15/1.57/2.15/2.63 and CBCL ADHD T-score SDs 6.17/5.98/5.58/5.62 at T1-T4, but these are total (between + within) SDs, and the coefficients are standardized on the within-person components. The resulting d's describe within-person lagged effects and are not directly comparable to between-person regression d's from other papers. M1 has no CIs in the PDF (they are in supplementary Tables S2/S3), so M1 d's have no CI. In M2, two male ADHD -> OSA CIs do not contain their point estimates and several male CIs are wider than SE implies; converting those CIs would give misleading d intervals. Completion pass (2026-10-01): set iv_type = continuous on M1 and M2; moved Table 3 SEs into the numeric 'se' field on every M2 estimate (exact p values were already numeric). M1 SE/CI/exact p confirmed absent from the PDF (supplementary Tables S2/S3 only; no supplement file in docs/pdfs). For the M2 male cells whose printed CIs are inconsistent with beta and SE, the SE and exact p offer an alternative CI basis (beta +/- 1.96*SE).

extraction_flags: 1) The M1 (full-sample RI-CLPM) point estimates come from the path labels in Fig. 1. Their SEs, CIs and exact p-values are in supplementary Tables S2/S3, which are not in the PDF, so M1 has no CIs and its significance is read from the asterisks. Fig. 1 was checked at high resolution, but each label's assignment to its path (for example, -0.009 is OSA T1->ADHD T2 and -0.006 is ADHD T1->OSA T2) should be confirmed against S2/S3. 2) Table 3 has printing problems in the male column. Two male ADHD->OSA CIs do not contain their own point estimates: -0.057 printed with [-0.029, -0.002], and -0.051 printed with [-0.040, -0.004]. Several other male CIs, such as -0.013 (SE 0.023) printed with [-0.253, 0.141], are much wider than 1.96*SE implies. They were copied as printed; do not convert those CIs without checking. 3) The between-person random-intercept correlation r = 0.068 is printed with '95% CI, 0.07-0.35', which does not contain 0.068, so the CI was left null. It is included in M1 as a beta_std cell. 4) The standardized coefficients are within-person (RI-CLPM), so the d's are not directly comparable to between-person d's. The Table 1 SDs are total SDs and were not used. 5) M2 (sex multigroup, Table 3) was extracted as a separate card because the authors interpret it. The paper does not say whether sex was dropped as a covariate in that model. 6) The content-type moderation (Tables S5-S7) and the non-imputed sensitivity analysis are supplement-only and were excluded for lack of numbers. 7) The SEM software is not named, and the OSA time units are implied hours/day but not stated explicitly. 8) OSA qualifies under FT-IC2 Step 2 (texting + social networking sites + video chat only). In the ADHD->OSA paths, OSA is the DV.
